body: What version of Prometheus are you using?

Sorry forgot to mention. 

It's current master 03b90b46 but happens also on `2.9.2`
The issue here is that your configuration is invalid, as you're producing two identical time series. That's checked down in PromQL, but not for the label addition in rules.

Yes, this is what I'm aware of as I wrote in the issue description, I know that it produces invalid data. 

The thing is first of all there is no warning in case of recording rules the same way it's for the label replace in the docs
> Care must be taken with labeldrop and labelkeep to ensure that metrics are still uniquely labeled once the labels are removed.

But the main thing is that Prometheus decides to use random value without letting user know about this. This is my main concern. Sorry if I didn't make myself clear before.

body: @brian-brazil @FUSAKLA can any of you close this issue, as this has been solved,
This issue has not been resolved.

@brian-brazil isn't this PR : https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/6025 solved the issue, and if it doesn't ,can you brief out about possible correction needed which can be implemented though!
That added a warning about something that can cause this to promtool. We still need to check for this and error out in the recording rule code.

I would like to work on this, as this issue has been silent for a little bit and it looks like a good first project. @brian-brazil it looks like I would put that in prometheus/rules/manager.go rather than a recording rule specific file though, yeah?
Yes, this would be around where we append the results to the tsdb.

By the time the result gets to the manager, the two series are already conflated into one, and we can't detect it anymore. This is the place in the recording rule code where the conflation without check is actually happening, and where a warning or similar should be logged: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/2d8b6c779299ee7e758d947ce990e69d61039a4c/rules/recording.go#L82-L95

Ah no, sorry, that part actually still returns two identical series to the caller, but then I don't understand why no debug warning is logged despite the code at https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/2d8b6c779299ee7e758d947ce990e69d61039a4c/rules/manager.go#L552-L554.

I tried setting `--log.level=debug`, but didn't get anything logged.

The bug seems to be here in the TSDB appender code that checks against the entire chunk max time instead of the individual series's last sample value time: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/2d8b6c779299ee7e758d947ce990e69d61039a4c/tsdb/head.go#L1781-L1783

It doesn't return an error on duplicate samples for the same timestamp.

EDIT: fixed code link.
@rothsa Want to give fixing that a shot? Happy to look at it together!
